title: Module 7 Vocabulary Check
intro: Answer each item. Feedback comes right away. Items you miss come back for a retry round.

items.q: We use a t statistic instead of z when
o: The population standard deviation is unknown and must be estimated from the sample
items.why: The sample standard deviation replaces sigma, which adds uncertainty. The t distribution captures that uncertainty.

items.q: The estimated standard error for a one-sample t is
o: s divided by the square root of n
sigma divided by the square root of n
s times the square root of n
items.why: It has the same form as the z standard error, with s in place of sigma.

items.q: Degrees of freedom for a one-sample t test are
items.why: df is the number of scores free to vary once the sample mean is fixed.

items.q: Compared with the normal distribution, the t distribution
o: Has heavier tails and approaches normal as df increases
items.why: With small df, extreme values are more likely, so critical values are larger.

items.q: As degrees of freedom increase, the critical t value
o: Gets smaller and approaches the z value
items.why: With df = 9 the two-tailed critical t at .05 is 2.262. With very large df it approaches 1.96.

items.q: A 95 percent confidence interval for mu is
o: M plus or minus t(critical) times the estimated standard error
M plus or minus 1.96 times s
items.why: Use the critical t for df, not z, because sigma is unknown.

items.q: If a 95 percent CI for the mean difference includes the null value, the two-tailed test at alpha = .05
items.why: The CI and the test agree. A null value inside the interval is a plausible value.

items.q: The t statistic is a ratio of
o: The obtained mean difference to the estimated standard error
items.why: It is how many estimated standard errors the sample mean is from the hypothesized mean.
